# greta.gp: Gaussian Process in `greta`

[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.gp/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta.gp/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![CRAN
status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/greta.gp)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=greta.gp)
[![Codecov test
coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/greta-dev/greta.gp/graph/badge.svg?token=sDr01k2p2r)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/greta-dev/greta.gp)

`greta.gp` extends greta to let you define Gaussian processes as part of
your model. It provides a syntax to create and combine GP kernels, and
use them to define either full rank or sparse Gaussian processes.

## Installation

You can install the current release version of `greta.gp` from CRAN:

``` r

install.packages("greta.gp")
```

Or install the development version of `greta.gp` from
[r-universe](https://greta-dev.r-universe.dev/):

``` r

install.packages("greta.gp", repos = "https://greta-dev.r-universe.dev")
```

You can also install the development version of `greta.gp` via GitHub:

``` r

remotes::install_github("greta-dev/greta.gp")
```

## Example usage

``` r

# simulate data
x <- runif(20, 0, 10)
y <- sin(x) + rnorm(20, 0, 0.5)
x_plot <- seq(-1, 11, length.out = 200)
```

``` r

library(greta)
library(greta.gp)

# hyperparameters
rbf_var <- lognormal(0, 1)
rbf_len <- lognormal(0, 1)
obs_sd <- lognormal(0, 1)

# kernel & GP
kernel <- rbf(rbf_len, rbf_var) + bias(1)
f <- gp(x, kernel)

# likelihood
distribution(y) <- normal(f, obs_sd)

# prediction
f_plot <- project(f, x_plot)
```

``` r

# fit the model by Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
m <- model(f_plot)
draws <- mcmc(m, n_samples = 250)
```

``` r

# plot 200 posterior samples
# plot 200 posterior samples
plot(
  y ~ x,
  pch = 16,
  col = grey(0.4),
  xlim = c(0, 10),
  ylim = c(-2.5, 2.5),
  las = 1,
  fg = grey(0.7),
)
for (i in 1:200) {
  lines(draws[[1]][i, ] ~ x_plot,
    lwd = 2,
    col = rgb(0.7, 0.1, 0.4, 0.1)
  )
}
```

![](reference/figures/README-plotting-1.png)

# Package index

## Gaussian process kernels

Create and combine covariance functions (kernels) to describe the
structure of a Gaussian process.

- [`bias()`](https://greta-dev.github.io/greta.gp/reference/kernels.md)
  [`constant()`](https://greta-dev.github.io/greta.gp/reference/kernels.md)
  [`white()`](https://greta-dev.github.io/greta.gp/reference/kernels.md)
  [`iid()`](https://greta-dev.github.io/greta.gp/reference/kernels.md)
  [`rbf()`](https://greta-dev.github.io/greta.gp/reference/kernels.md)
  [`rational_quadratic()`](https://greta-dev.github.io/greta.gp/reference/kernels.md)
  [`linear()`](https://greta-dev.github.io/greta.gp/reference/kernels.md)
  [`polynomial()`](https://greta-dev.github.io/greta.gp/reference/kernels.md)
  [`expo()`](https://greta-dev.github.io/greta.gp/reference/kernels.md)
  [`mat12()`](https://greta-dev.github.io/greta.gp/reference/kernels.md)
  [`mat32()`](https://greta-dev.github.io/greta.gp/reference/kernels.md)
  [`mat52()`](https://greta-dev.github.io/greta.gp/reference/kernels.md)
  [`cosine()`](https://greta-dev.github.io/greta.gp/reference/kernels.md)
  [`periodic()`](https://greta-dev.github.io/greta.gp/reference/kernels.md)
  : Gaussian process kernels

## Gaussian processes

Define full rank or sparse Gaussian processes from kernels, and project
a fitted process to new coordinates.

- [`gp()`](https://greta-dev.github.io/greta.gp/reference/gp.md)
  [`project()`](https://greta-dev.github.io/greta.gp/reference/gp.md) :
  Define a Gaussian process

## Package

- [`greta.gp-package`](https://greta-dev.github.io/greta.gp/reference/greta.gp.md)
  [`greta.gp`](https://greta-dev.github.io/greta.gp/reference/greta.gp.md)
  : Gaussian process modelling in greta
